newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's privatisation plan makes $2.0 billion.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's privatisation plan makes $2.0 billion.

text.p: Kuwait has raised about 600 million dinars ($2.0 billion) from its privatisation plan launched in 1994, Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) director-general Ali al-Bader was quoted as saying on Saturday.
Bader, quoted by al-Rai as-Aam newspaper, also said the KIA had decided to stop offering shares on the Kuwait Stock Exchange because of criticism made against this method of privatisation.
"Total sales under the privatisation plan...stood at some 600 million dinars," Badersaid.
The programme, announced after the 1991 Gulf War and launched in 1994, is designed to widen the investor base, reduce state economic controls and boost efficiency.
Dealers said they were concerned about possible share price falls after KIA stock offerings on the Kuwait Stock Exchange recently.
Bader said KIA sales through direct offerings were "very little" -- 94 million dinars since the programme started.
But he said: "In the light of remarks made against this method in the past period KIA has decided to stop using it."
Most of the state share selloffs were carried out through auctions and public subscriptions.

KIA, which has already sold its stake in about 15 Kuwaiti firms, is in charge of a plan to sell state holdings in about 60 local firms and to prepare for a second phase to end state involvement in some public services like water, electricity and telecommunications.
Participation in Kuwait's privatisation plan is exclusive to nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council -- Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait.
